name: DataTable
description: Interactive table — sort, select, expand, and click through rows of data.

dependencies.name: @tanstack/react-table
dependencies.reason: Optional — powers sorting, selection, and expansion; without it DataTable renders a static, non-interactive table.

propsSummary: columns: ColumnDef[] - column definitions
data: T[] - row data array
sortable: boolean - enable sorting
selectable: boolean - enable row selection
showCheckbox: boolean - add checkbox column
getSubRows: (row) => T[] - enable expandable rows
onRowClick: (row, event) => void - row activation handler with event access
getRowProps: (row) => HTMLAttributes<HTMLTableRowElement> - row-level ARIA, role, data, class, and event props
emptyState: ReactNode - EmptyState parts for an empty result
loading / skeletonRows - placeholder rows under the real header
error / onRetry / retryLabel - the error box for a failed load
bordered: boolean - the sheet (surface plane, hairline, surface radius)
maxHeight: number | string - bound the height; rows scroll inside and the head sticks
wrapperClassName / wrapperProps - style and configure the outer wrapper div

getRowId.description: Unique key extractor for each row

showCheckbox.description: Show checkbox column for row selection

getRowProps.description: Props applied to each rendered data row. Use this for row-level ARIA labels, roles, and data attributes.

getSubRows.description: Extract sub-rows from a row for expandable tree tables

emptyState.description:
What an empty result says: EmptyState parts (`EmptyState.Title`,
`EmptyState.Description`, `EmptyState.Actions`) rendered in a compact
EmptyState under the real header. Defaults to a one-line "No data".

loading.description: When true, render placeholder rows (one bar per cell) instead of data.

skeletonRows.description: Number of placeholder rows to show while loading (default 6).

error.description:
A failed load: what went wrong and what to do, shown in an error box
under the real header. Ignored while `loading`.

onRetry.description: Retry the failed load. Shows a retry button in the error box.

hideHeader.description: Hide the column header row (e.g. stacked per-group tables share one).

caption.description: Visible caption for the table (recommended for accessibility)

captionHidden.description: Hide the caption visually but keep it for screen readers

bordered.description: Draw the sheet: the surface plane, a hairline border and the surface radius

maxHeight.description: Bound the table's height: the rows scroll inside it and the head sticks

wrapperClassName.description: Additional class name for the outer wrapper div

wrapperProps.description: Props forwarded to the outer wrapper div

when: Rows need sorting, selection, or expansion
Users scan and compare several attributes per row
A row click opens the record behind it
whenNot: The data is read-only and static (use Table)
Each item is a single line (use List)
Narrow screens where a card list reads better
guidelines: Cap visible columns near 5–7; push the rest behind a row click
Always set emptyState — a bare grid reads as broken
Pass error and onRetry for a failed load; loading wins over error, error over empty
Clickable rows need getRowProps for a role and an accessible name
Every row is the 32px control track; there is no density or stripe option
accessibility: Headers stay real th elements with scope
Sortable headers are buttons — reachable by keyboard
Selection checkboxes carry their own labels

dont.reason: Do not use DataTable for a simple static comparison.

examples.name: Default
examples.description: Columns and data are the only required props; everything else is opt-in.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
          ]}
          data={[
            { name: "Ada Lovelace", status: "Active" },
            { name: "Grace Hopper", status: "Pending" },
          ]}
          aria-label="Team members"
        />

examples.name: Loading
examples.description: Placeholder rows, one bar per cell, sit under the real header so the page never jumps.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
          ]}
          data={[]}
          loading
          skeletonRows={3}
          aria-label="Loading team members"
        />

examples.name: Rich Cells
examples.description: A cell renderer drops any component — avatar, badge — straight into the column.
examples.code: ( {row.original.name} ), }, { accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" }, { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: ({ row }) => ( {row.original.status} ), }, ]} data={[ { name: "Ada Lovelace", role: "Engineer", status: "Active" }, { name: "Grace Hopper", role: "Admiral", status: "Pending" }, ]} bordered aria-label="Team members" />

examples.name: Sortable
examples.description: Click a header to sort; click it again to reverse.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "amount", header: "Amount" },
          ]}
          data={[
            { name: "Subscription", amount: "$24.00" },
            { name: "Usage", amount: "$12.00" },
          ]}
          sortable
          bordered
          caption="Recent transactions"
          captionHidden
          aria-label="Transactions"
        />

examples.name: Checkbox Selection
examples.description: The header checkbox toggles every row at once.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
          ]}
          data={[
            { id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace", status: "Active" },
            { id: "grace", name: "Grace Hopper", status: "Pending" },
          ]}
          getRowId={(row) => row.id}
          selectable
          showCheckbox
          bordered
          aria-label="Team members"
        />

examples.name: Expandable Rows
examples.description: Children fold away under their parent, like a file tree; depth shows by indent alone.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "type", header: "Type" },
          ]}
          data={[
            {
              id: "src",
              name: "src",
              type: "folder",
              subRows: [{ id: "components", name: "components", type: "folder", subRows: [] }],
            },
            { id: "package", name: "package.json", type: "file", subRows: [] },
          ]}
          getRowId={(row) => row.id}
          getSubRows={(row) => row.subRows}
          bordered
          aria-label="File tree"
        />

examples.name: With Filters
examples.description: Filter controls sit outside the table; you own the filtering.
examples.code:
<Stack gap="sm">
          <Input type="search" aria-label="Search users" placeholder="Search..." />
          <DataTable
            columns={[
              { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
              { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
            ]}
            data={[{ name: "Ada Lovelace", status: "Active" }]}
            sortable
            bordered
            emptyState={
              <EmptyState.Title as="p">No users match the current filters</EmptyState.Title>
            }
            aria-label="Filtered team members"
          />
        </Stack>

examples.name: Clickable Rows
examples.description: Mouse or keyboard opens the row; getRowProps supplies its name.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "method", header: "Method" },
            { accessorKey: "path", header: "Path" },
          ]}
          data={[{ method: "GET", path: "/v1/components" }]}
          getRowProps={(row) => ({
            role: "button",
            "aria-label": `Open ${row.method} ${row.path}`,
          })}
          onRowClick={() => undefined}
          aria-label="API endpoints"
        />

examples.name: Empty State
examples.description: A compact EmptyState replaces the rows and keeps the headers in place.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
          ]}
          data={[]}
          emptyState={
            <>
              <EmptyState.Title>No users match your search</EmptyState.Title>
              <EmptyState.Description>Try a shorter name or clear a filter.</EmptyState.Description>
            </>
          }
          aria-label="Search results"
        />

examples.name: Error
examples.description: A failed load shows the error box under the real header, with one way out.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
          ]}
          data={[]}
          error="The team list did not load. Check your connection, then retry."
          onRetry={() => undefined}
          aria-label="Team members"
        />

examples.name: Long Cell Content
examples.description: Oversized values scroll inside the table instead of stretching the page.
examples.code:
<DataTable
          columns={[
            { accessorKey: "name", header: "Administrator" },
            { accessorKey: "status", header: "Recovery policy" },
          ]}
          data={[
            {
              name: "A very long localized administrator identity that remains distinguishable",
              status:
                "Pending confirmation of the detailed workspace recovery policy and notification workflow",
            },
          ]}
          bordered
          aria-label="Long localized team member data"
        />

relations.note: Use Table for simple semantic HTML tables
Use EmptyState for empty table states
